Question_text: Warm blooded animals need to maintain a constant internal body temperature. In cold weather some of these animals crowd together in groups. Some students used test-tubes containing hot water to represent animals in an investigation into the loss of heat from animals' bodies. One test-tube, A, represented one animal on its own, as shown in Fig. 1.1. Another test-tube, B, represented an animal surrounded by seven similar animals in a group, as shown in Fig. 1.2. Test-tube C represented one of the outer animals in the group, as shown in Fig. 1.2.
On the grid below, plot the results for the three test-tubes A, B and C on the axes.
Describe and compare the temperature changes in each of the three test-tubes.
Suggest and explain two ways to improve this method to make the result reliable.
State which test-tube represents the animal that finds it easiest to maintain a constant body temperature.
Suggest how animals crowding together in a group can help them to maintain body temperature in cold weather.
